title: AI models up to
17x cheaper.
Check this first.
slides.subtitle: Open-weight models like DeepSeek are listed far below Claude per token. Here is what to test before you move any work across.

slides.label: The price gap
slides.detail: Per million tokens, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is listed at $0.15 in and $0.60 out off-peak. Claude Sonnet 5 is $2 and $10. Roughly 7 to 17 times cheaper, depending on the time of day.
slides.start: Check each provider's own pricing page today. These rates move and sources disagree.

slides.label: What it means in pounds
slides.detail: On 5 million tokens in and 1 million out, about $2.70 against $20. Real money only at high volume, such as sorting every enquiry or summarising every call.
slides.start: Estimate your monthly volume before you get excited about the saving.

slides.label: Cheap is not cheap per task
slides.detail: One benchmark found the cheapest model per solved task was not the top scorer. Retries and wrong answers eat the saving.
slides.start: Measure cost per finished job on your own work, not per token.

slides.label: Where your data goes
slides.detail: DeepSeek's own policy says data is stored in China. A UK firm sending personal data through the API would likely be the exporter and needs a transfer risk assessment.
slides.start: Ask any provider where the servers are and whether prompts are kept or used for training.

slides.label: Check the licence
slides.detail: Open-weight is not open source. Some licences limit commercial use or set revenue thresholds. We could not confirm DeepSeek Flash's licence from our sources.
slides.start: Read the licence on the model's own page before you build on it.

slides.label: Test on safe jobs first
slides.detail: Drafts from public facts, price lists, product descriptions. Run ten real examples through both models, names removed, and score each one yourself out of five.
slides.start: Pick one routine job with no customer data and run the ten-example test this week.

title: Test it on safe work.
Then decide.
slides.body: We have not run a client workload on these models yet, so this is how we would approach it, not a verdict. Prices are tool costs and will change.
slides.cta: Which job in your business could you hand to a cheaper model tomorrow without a single customer name in the prompt?
